Real-Time Benchmark & Big-O Curves

Compares active Indexed Min-Heap vs periodic Full Sort vs Lazy Deletion.

💡 Plain-English Verdict

Indexed Min-Heap maintains the Top-K dynamically in O(log K) per sale. For a stream of N events, it costs only O(N log K), whereas periodic Sorting costs O(N · U log U). When K is small (e.g. K=10) and U is large (e.g. U=100,000), the Indexed Min-Heap is up to 100x faster!

Why Standard Heaps Fail (std::priority_queue)

Standard binary heaps lack an index lookup map (pos), causing updated elements to become stale and out-of-order.

❌ Standard Heap

When product count increases, std::priority_queue cannot locate it in O(1). It either leaves the node in the wrong position (violating the invariant) or pushes duplicate stale nodes.

Root: B (Count: 2) [STALE!]

✅ Indexed Min-Heap

Maintains unordered_map pos. When count updates, updateKey(id) immediately locates index in O(1) and executes siftDown/siftUp in O(log K).
